name: relation_folded_directory
scope_warning: Measured on five small covering fixtures (1,064 to 80,840 directory rows) on a single host with three local Semi parties, one query per run. The per-query figures for the full evaluation fixtures are EXTRAPOLATIONS from a fitted line, not runs: the WebQSP eval projection is a 21x reach beyond the largest fixture actually executed. The speedup ratio is a property of the layout (relation count and frontier width) and does not transfer to a layout with different ones.
headline_finding: Hop two was re-resolving the same relation once per frontier address. Folding the relation out of the directory before reading it cuts communication 5.7x on the largest WebQSP fixture measured, with byte-identical output, no new public parameter and no change to the threat model.

the_waste.observed: The directory is 97.7% of per-address cost on WebQSP and 81.8% on MetaQA.
the_waste.cause: read_directory demuxes the combined address entity*relation_count + relation-1 over the whole dense keyspace, so each of the FRONTIER_SLOTS hop-two addresses scanned entity_count * relation_count rows.
the_waste.the_observation: Every hop-two address carries the SAME relation_2 -- only the entity differs. The relation was being resolved once per address instead of once per query.

the_change.what: Contract the relation out of the directory once per query, leaving a table indexed by entity alone; each frontier address then scans entity_count rows.
the_change.cost_law: n * E * R  ->  E * R + n * E, a factor of n*R/(R+n)
the_change.why_it_is_free: A pure re-association of the same sum: the same products over the same shares, grouped differently. No new public parameter, no change to the leakage function L, no change to the corruption threshold, no new trust assumption.
the_change.hop_one_deliberately_not_folded: Hop one has one address per relation, so there is nothing to amortise and folding would add E products per query for no return.
the_change.ablation_switch: --ablate-folded-directory restores the unfolded read. It is a renderer argument, never a configuration field, and program_name separates the two variants so an A/B run cannot silently reuse one compiled circuit.

measured.protocol: MP-SPDZ Semi, three local parties. Threat model unchanged: any two of three servers may collude.
measured.note: MB figures are global data sent, all parties, one query.
measured.the_ratio_grows_with_size: 3.35x -> 4.69x -> 5.68x across the three WebQSP fixtures, because a fixed ~3 GB floor dilutes the headline at small sizes. The fitted per-row term is the honest measure of the change.

correctness.method: All output values reconstructed from all three party logs (3-of-3 additive shares summed mod 2^127-1) under both circuits and compared.
correctness.result: IDENTICAL on every arm, 16 values each.
correctness.why_this_matters: The claim is that folding is semantically a no-op. That is checked against the preserved unfolded circuit, not asserted from the algebra.

fitted_cost_law.webqsp_unfolded: 2,992 MB + 0.8297 MB per directory row (3 points)
fitted_cost_law.webqsp_folded: 3,197 MB + 0.1129 MB per directory row (3 points)
fitted_cost_law.metaqa_unfolded: 352 MB + 0.2412 MB per directory row (3 points)
fitted_cost_law.metaqa_folded: 364 MB + 0.1297 MB per directory row (2 points only -- weaker fit)
fitted_cost_law.consistency_check: After folding, the per-row slopes of the two datasets converge (0.113 vs 0.130) where before they differed 3.4x. That is the expected signature: what remains per row is the dataset-independent hop-one scan plus the fold, while the removed term carried the frontier-width factor, which is 15 on WebQSP and 9 on MetaQA.

projections_NOT_runs.caveat: Both are extrapolations from the fitted line. The largest fixture actually executed was 80,840 rows, so the WebQSP figure is a 21x reach and should be treated as an order-of-magnitude statement.

what_this_does_NOT_establish: NOT a claim that the cost is now practical. 191 GB per query on the WebQSP eval fixture is a projection, and it is still far above any publishable per-query cost.
NOT a change to asymptotics. The directory is still dense in entities x relations, so cost still grows with the product of the two. This removes a frontier-width FACTOR, not the dense-keyspace TERM.
NOT a full-graph result. Nothing here was run at WebQSP or MetaQA scale.
NOT a retrieval-quality result. Output is byte-identical, so quality is unchanged by construction -- that is the point, not a separate finding.
NOT applicable to hop one, which is unchanged and still pays a full dense scan per query.
NOT a malicious-security or sublinear-access result.
what_is_still_on_the_table: The dense entity x relation directory is 2.20% occupied on the WebQSP eval fixture and 0.154% at full scale. A compact table sized to the actual key count would attack the dense-keyspace term itself rather than a factor of it. Not implemented and not measured; the ratios above say nothing about whether it would work.
